scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #5091: PC1 (10.1.0.100) and the other VLAN 10 hosts in Office A report
their default gateway (10.1.0.1) is intermittently unreachable -- it eventually
responds but latency is high. VLAN 40 (Laptop1) and VLAN 99 are unaffected.
The on-site tech swapped the patch cable and is now convinced the access switch
aswa2 has failed and is dropping frames intermittently; they want approval to
replace aswa2. Please confirm the aswa2 hardware failure and identify the port.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-dswa1-vlan10-svi-down: the VLAN 10 SVI
(br10, 10.1.0.2/24) on dswa1 is administratively down. dswa1 is the VRRP MASTER
for the VLAN 10 VIP 10.1.0.1 (priority 105); when its br10 SVI goes down,
keepalived on dswa1 stops sending VRRP advertisements and dswa2 (BACKUP,
priority 1) eventually takes over the VIP. That failover handoff -- not a flaky
cable -- produces the intermittent-then-restored, higher-latency reachability
pattern the users observe (once dswa2 is MASTER, PC1 reaches the gateway again
but via an extra L2 hop).

The TWIST: the ticket blames aswa2 and asks to replace it. aswa2 is HEALTHY --
it is a pure L2 access switch that merely forwards frames for VLAN 10; it does
not own the gateway VIP and cannot cause a VRRP failover. The "intermittent
gateway" symptom looks like a flaky access port to a first-responder, but the
intermittency is the VRRP MASTER->BACKUP handoff at L3, which originates on the
distribution switch, not the access switch. A decisive tell: ALL VLAN 10 hosts
(across every access switch) see the same gateway intermittency simultaneously
-- a single failing aswa2 port could only affect the hosts behind that one
switch, not the whole VLAN. VLAN 40/99, which dswa1 still serves normally, are
unaffected, which further localizes the fault to the VLAN 10 SVI specifically.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = dswa1 (VLAN 10 SVI / br10
down). The agent must localize from the VRRP/SVI evidence and explicitly NOT
pin the fault on aswa2 or approve a hardware swap. An agent that "confirms the
aswa2 failure" has followed the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix:
`ip link set br10 up` on dswa1.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1
scoring_axes: must-identify-svi-gateway-down: VLAN 10 SVI / br10 down causing VRRP MASTER->BACKUP failover
bonus-exonerates-aswa2: notes aswa2 is a healthy L2 access switch and does not own the gateway VIP

agent.diagnosis_text:
No hardware fault found on aswa2. The intermittent reachability to the VLAN 10 default gateway is caused by a Spanning Tree control-plane issue on the aswa2 uplinks, not by a bad switch or port.

Evidence:
- aswa2 STP: eth1 is the root port toward dswa1, but its message age timer sits at ~19.7s (max-age 20s) across samples and does not reset, indicating BPDUs from the root are not reliably received (brctl showstp br0 on aswa2). eth2 is blocking. dswa1 is clearly the STP root (priority 4096).
- aswa2 VLAN trunking: eth1 and eth2 have no PVID/native VLAN configured (bridge -d vlan show). With vlan_filtering enabled, untagged STP BPDUs may be dropped on ports without a PVID, causing BPDU loss and periodic STP re-convergence. This produces brief blackholes/latency spikes to 10.1.0.1 (which resides on dswa2), matching the “intermittent high latency to gateway” reports on VLAN 10.
- No hardware symptoms: aswa2 uplinks show link up, zero errors/drops (ethtool, ip -s link), and normal forwarding states otherwise. Pings from hosts succeed when topology is stable.

Mechanism: Missing PVID on trunk ports prevents reliable receipt of untagged STP BPDUs on aswa2, so the root-port BPDU ages out, triggering STP transitions and transient traffic loss to the VLAN 10 gateway via the DSW peer path.

Localization: aswa2 br0 STP on uplink eth1 (to dswa1); eth2 is the alternate blocked link.

Root cause: aswa2 trunk ports are misconfigured with no native VLAN/PVID, causing BPDU loss and STP instability.

Corrective fix: Configure a PVID/native VLAN on aswa2 eth1 and eth2 (and match on dswa1/dswa2 trunks), e.g., add VLAN 1 or 99 as PVID/untagged, so STP BPDUs are accepted. No switch replacement is needed.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-svi-gateway-down: VLAN 10 SVI / br10 down causing VRRP MASTER->BACKUP failover
per_axis.rationale: The agent attributes the issue to STP on aswa2 and does not identify the VLAN 10 SVI (br10) on dswa1 being administratively down and causing the VRRP MASTER->BACKUP failover.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-aswa2: notes aswa2 is a healthy L2 access switch and does not own the gateway VIP
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states no hardware fault on aswa2, treats it as a pure L2 access switch, and indicates the gateway VIP is on a distribution device (not aswa2), thereby exonerating aswa2 from being the VIP owner or needing replacement.
The proposed remediation (set PVIDs/native VLANs on aswa2 uplinks) does not match the expected fix (bring up br10 on dswa1) and would not correct the reported fault.

The agent's writeup asserts STP/BPDU and PVID misconfiguration on aswa2 as the root cause, but the investigation log does not provide clear, unambiguous evidence for those specific claims and crucial checks (SVI/VRRP/br10 state on the distribution switches) are missing or contradict the explanation (e.g. keepalived inactive). The reasoning therefore contains unsupported leaps and omits key diagnostics needed to justify blaming aswa2.
